entries.title: Judges 13:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Israel is delivered into the hands of Philistines. 2 An angel appears to Manoah's wife. 8 The angel appears to Manoah. 15 Manoah's sacrifices, whereby the angel is discovered. 24 Samson is born.

entries.title: Judges 13:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
A man. De 33:1; Jos 14:6; 1Sa 2:27; 9:6; 1Ki 17:18,24; 2Ki 4:9,16 1Ti 6:11 countenance was. Mt 28:3; Lu 9:29; Ac 6:15 terrible. 22; Ge 28:16,17; Ex 3:2,6; Da 8:17; 10:5,11; Mt 28:4; Re 1:17 but I asked, etc.The Vulgate renders this cause very differently, the negative Not being omitted: {Quem c�m interrog�ssim quis esset, et unde venisset, et quo nomine vocaretur, noluit mihi dicere; sed hoc respondit, etc; "Whom when I asked who he was, and whence he came, and by what name he was called, would not tell me: but this he said," etc. The negative is also wanting in the Septuagint, as it is in the Complutensian Polyglott; [kai erouton auton pothen estin, kai to onoma auton, ouk apengeilen moi.] "And I asked him whence he was, and his name, but he did not tell me." This is also the reading of the Codex Alexandrinus; but the Septuagint in the London Polyglott, the Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic, read the negative particle with the Hebrew text: I asked Not his name, etc.

his name. 17,18; Ge 32:29; Lu 1:19

entries.title: Judges 13:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Behold. Joh 1:41,42; 4:28,29 the other day.{Byyom,} rather, "in this day," or "to-day," for the word other is not in the original, and it is probably that the angel appeared in the morning and evening of the same day.

entries.content: How shall we order the child. Heb. what shall be the mannerof the child? Ge 18:19; Pr 4:4; 22:6; Eph 6:4 how shall we do unto him. or, what shall he do? Heb. whatshall be his work?

entries.title: Judges 13:16
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
I will not.As I am a spiritual being, I subsist not by earthly food; and cannot partake of your bounty.

and if, etc.Rather, "but if thou wilt offer," etc.

unto thee. 23; 6:26

entries.title: Judges 13:18
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Why askest. 6; Ge 32:29 secret. or, wonderful.It was because his name was secret that Manoah wished to know it. But the angel does not say it was secret, but {hoo pailee,} "it is wonderful;" the very character given to the Messiah: "His name shall be called {pailai,} Wonderful," Isa 9:6.

entries.title: Judges 13:19
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
took. 6:19,20; 1Ki 18:30-38 did wondrously.He acted according to His Name: He, being wonderful, performed wonders; probably causing fire to arise out of the rock and consume the sacrifice, and then ascended in the flame.
